input.d8_retired_2026_08_21: The d8 half graded support-matrix D8 while D8 was an OPEN wall-clock breach: it recomputed the published range from the reports the row cited and required the row to cite them. M12 (PR #20, ADR-013) then CLOSED D8 — the row no longer publishes a breach range, so there is nothing left for this half to recompute, and it was failing on a row that had legitimately changed rather than on a defect. Retired rather than re-pointed because the number it protected is now gated directly and better: `fast-wall-clock-budget` asserts the suite's own wall clock against the ceiling (60s local, 80s CI) and `wall-clock-probe-history-isolated` covers the history side, so a regression reddens the gate itself instead of a prose range. The reports it cited (20260821-215759/215923-fast.json) were measured pre-M12 and are now uncited; they are prune candidates under ADR-012. The README-counts half stays — nothing else derives those, and it reddens the moment a case is added.

provenance: PR #21 review, R6 (MEDIUM) and R5 (MEDIUM) — the same class twice: a number in a document of record that this branch's own committed artifacts contradict. README said 91 fast / 101 total while the runner said 93 fast / 103 files (the edit added +5 for the new cases and carried a pre-existing -1 forward). D8 said `71.3-76.5s at M9 with five more cases` while the four fast reports committed in the same PR measure 79.01-79.75s with six more cases — understating a declared budget breach by ~3.4s, on the row M12 is keyed to. Neither number is re-typed here: the suite sizes come from `evals.run.load_cases`, the runner's own discovery, and the D8 range is recomputed from the `wall_seconds` of the reports the row cites. Watched red against the pre-fix documents: `readme_does_not_say: 'offline gate: 95 cases, zero paid calls'` and `d8_range: {the_cited_reports_show: '79.0-79.8s'}`. PR #23 R4 added the "Where it stands" half: the same commit that fixed the three graded count lines to 102/112 left the block beside them publishing `20260821-224446-fast.json` — `fast 98/98  invariant 30/30  59.4s`, a pre-merge run at a main-only sha — while the branch committed 102-result and 34-result reports at its own head. Ungraded prose next to graded prose drifts on the first merge. Watched red against that README: `readme_does_not_cite: 20260822-010408-fast.json` plus `readme_does_not_say: fast  102/102` / `invariant  34/34` / `59.6s`. Extended at M29 (`docs/analysis.md` §8a-3, `specs/decisions/ADR-015-a-freeze.md`): ADR-015's own header and criterion 5 asserted 'criterion 5 is now green offline, with live re-confirmation ... pending' and INDEX.md's one-liner said 'criterion 5 green offline with live re-confirmation pending redeploy' — both true when written, both falsified by the post-merge probe this milestone committed in the same document tree. Watched red against the pre-amendment files (git stash of this PR's ADR-015/INDEX.md edits): `asserts_criterion5_green: 'criterion 5 is now green'` (from both `specs/decisions/ADR-015-a-freeze.md` and `specs/decisions/INDEX.md`) and `asserts_criterion5_green: 'criterion 5 green offline'` (INDEX.md). The forbidden-phrase scan strips `~~struck~~` spans first, on purpose — ADR-015's own amendment convention (this ADR's citation of the plan's criterion-7 precedent) keeps the falsified original wording struck rather than deleted, and a naive substring scan would flag that preserved history forever; only prose asserting green OUTSIDE a strikethrough trips it.

triage.note: tagged invariant — a hand-maintained count is wrong again by the next milestone, and this repo has already burned a review round on three documents carrying three different totals for the same thing (PR #15, R19). The failure mode this closes is not the wrong number, it is the number that nothing recomputes. Adding a case to the suite now turns this red until README is updated, which is the intended cost. D8's cited reports are immutable artifacts, so its assertion is stable; moving the range means citing the runs it was measured from. The block cites report files rather than recomputing 'the latest run' on purpose: a report is immutable, so the assertion is stable, and moving the block means citing the runs it was measured from — the same contract D8's retired half had. The M29 half is the same shape one level up: a milestone's own ADR asserted its gate criterion was green-pending, and the milestone after it is the one that knows whether pending resolved true or false — nothing forced that resolution back into the ADR until this case checked for it.
